description:
FILED s473r (2026-09-07) closing #883`s open arm: the flattener`s per-element
cost, re-measured, plus the bench row it needs.

MEASURED (s473r, box load 1.5):

    my @a = (1..1000); sub f { return scalar(@_) }
    for (1..20000) { $s += f(@a) }          # 20 M elements flattened

    perl  0.02 s   -- perl ALIASES @a into @_; there is no per-element work
    PCL   0.35 s   -- minus 0.18 s for the same program calling `f(1)`
                   = 0.17 s / 20 M elements = 8.5 ns per element

`p-flatten-args` does, per element of a raw vector argument: a three-way
`cond` (null -> %p-defelem-box, p-box-p -> itself, else %p-elem-cell) and one
`vector-push-extend`.  The %p-elem-cell PROMOTION is amortised -- an array
converges to all-boxed after its first flatten -- so the steady-state cost is
the cond plus the push.

TWO THINGS ARE NEEDED BEFORE ANY FIX, and neither exists:

 1. A BENCH ROW.  `feread2`, the row #883 was sized against, no longer reaches
    the flattener at all: `for my $x (@a, @b)` takes the `foreach-arrays` run
    (#1184/#1409) and `grep -c p-flatten-args` on its emission is 0.  The row
    to add is the `f(@a)` shape above -- name it `feargs`, N_big 20 000 with a
    1000-element array, verified against perl like every other row.  Note that
    perl is O(1) on it, so the row is a RATIO outlier by construction and must
    be read as absolute seconds (plan Â§A.0).

 2. A PER-ARRAY "EVERY ELEMENT IS A BOX" FACT.  The only shape that beats the
    per-element cond is a bulk `replace` of the source store into the result,
    and that is legal only when no element needs transforming.  Testing it
    costs a scan of the same elements unless the array RECORDS it -- the
    #1140 raw-element machinery already carries a per-array raw flag, so the
    complement is the natural place.

DO NOT RETRY (measured and killed in #883): pre-sizing the result vector from
the element count.  It taxes the overwhelmingly common SCALAR-argument call to
save growth in the rare array one -- fib(27)x +3.8 %, gcdrec +2.3 % against
feread2 -2.1 %, net negative.  The rejection is recorded in a comment above
p-flatten-args.
================================================================
HALF 1 IS DONE (s473v, 2026-09-17) -- THE ROW EXISTS AND CARRIES A NUMBER.

`feargs` is in tools/bench-exec.pl (the exact program this task specified:
20 000 calls of `fargs(@a)` over a 1000-element array = 20 M elements
flattened; the callee returns scalar(@_) so the flattened list is CONSUMED,
and the sum is printed so both engines must agree).  It is verified against
perl like every other row.

MEASURED on a quiet box (load 2.0, 16 cores, main 2f9cc300 + the s473v
levers, gen v2-1480), two independent best-of-5 runs minutes apart:

    bench       perl(s)     pcl(s)   pcl/perl
    feargs      0.0242      0.1805     7.46x
    feargs      0.0228      0.1813     7.96x
    (control, same window: feread2 perl 0.4448 / pcl 0.1325 = 0.30x)

READ IT AS ABSOLUTE SECONDS, not as the ratio: perl ALIASES @a into @_ and is
O(1) in the array length, so the ratio is an outlier BY CONSTRUCTION (the same
reading rule the `pack` rows carry, plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md SS A.0).

    PCL  0.181 s / 20 M elements = 9.0 ns per element
    perl 0.023 s                  (no per-element work at all)

That confirms the s473r sizing (8.5 ns per element, measured there by
subtracting an `f(1)` program) from the other direction, on the row itself and
with startup subtracted -- and it is what the lever must beat.

HALF 2 IS STILL OPEN and is unchanged: `p-flatten-args` needs a per-array
"every element is a box" FACT before a bulk `replace` can beat the per-element
cond + vector-push-extend.  The #1140 raw-element machinery already carries a
per-array raw flag; the complement is the natural place.  The pre-sizing arm
stays KILLED (measured and rejected in #883; the rejection is a comment above
p-flatten-args).

================================================================
=== HALF TWO DONE (s473x, 2026-09-19, Opus) â AND THE FACT IT WAS WAITING FOR
=== TURNED OUT NOT TO BE NEEDED ===

sb-sprof :cpu over the `feargs` row itself (N=300 000, 3 227 samples,
scratch/s473x/prof.pl in the s473x worktree) splits the 91.9 % that is
`p-flatten-args`:

    reading the SOURCE array through its ARRAY HEADER          33.6 %
      (slow-hairy-data-vector-ref 12.9 + vector-hairy-data-vector-ref 11.2
       + (optimized-data-vector-ref t) 9.5)
    growing the RESULT one element at a time                  ~36 %
      (prepare-vector-push-extend 13.4 self / 31.1 total, extend-vector
       7.1 / 17.6, reallocate-vector-with-widetag 0.9 / 7.6,
       %DATA-VECTOR-AND-INDEX 4.7)
    GENERIC-+ (the index arithmetic of both)                    7.8 %
    p-flatten-args self (the loop and the three-way cond)      21.4 %
    %make-p-box â THE ELEMENT PROMOTION                         0.2 %

The promotion this task's design is about is 0.2 %: it really is amortised to
nothing.  Two thirds of the row is MACHINERY, and both halves of it go away
with no new fact at all:

  * ONE `%p-flatten-grow` per ARRAY argument (make room for its length, advance
    the fill pointer) instead of a capacity test per element.  This is NOT
    #883's rejected pre-sizing: nothing is measured, grown or pre-passed for a
    SCALAR argument, which is the call this function overwhelmingly serves, so
    the trade that killed that arm does not arise.
  * ONE `replace` through `%p-vec-data`'s simple-vectors (the s458ak element-
    storage idiom, contract already written) instead of a hairy `aref` per
    element, then a PATCH pass over the run that touches only the slots which
    are not already boxes â one SVREF and one type test each, and at steady
    state it changes nothing.
  * `%p-flatten-vector-slow` keeps the old element-at-a-time spread for a
    vector that is not the plain shape (displaced, specialised).  Identical
    elements in identical slots; the bulk path is a speed decision, never a
    semantic one.

MEASURED (BENCH_RT_B = the 4c6565e5 runtime, so ONE emission against two
cores, interleaved, best-of-5, controls in the same window; box shared, 1-min
load printed):

    bench          perl(s)    pclA(s)    pclB(s)       B/A    A/perl   (was)
    feargs          0.0224     0.0551     0.1854   +236.6%     2.46x   8.23x
    feargs (2nd)    0.0248     0.0548     0.1942   +254.0%     2.21x
    fib(27)x        1.4583     0.4253     0.4426     +4.1%     control
    gcdrec          0.1874     0.0968     0.0946     -2.2%     control
    subret          0.2062     0.0825     0.0812     -1.6%     control
    methret         0.0900     0.0950     0.0950     +0.0%     control
    feread2         0.4340     0.1286     0.1303     +1.3%     control

    0.1854 -> 0.0551 s = 9.0 ns -> 2.7 ns per element, 8.2x perl -> 2.5x.

The three scalar-argument control rows (`fib(27)x`, `gcdrec`, `subret`) are the
ones that killed #883's arm and they do not move.  The negative control band
(-2 %..-7 %) is CORE LAYOUT: a runtime carrying these new functions with the
ORIGINAL call site reproduces it (intloop+= -7.4 %, gcdrec -2.5 %, slices
-2.3 %, arrfill -2.1 %) and reads `feargs` +0.7 % â the s473r discriminator.

CORRECTNESS: guard `Pl/t/perf-levers-05.t` (63 rows, 0.53 s) â 15 flatten ANSWER
rows, every expectation perl 5.40.3's own output (count, order, a scalar before
and after, the same array twice, an empty array, `$_[0]`/`$_[2]` writing
THROUGH, holes reading undef and staying non-exists, a write through a hole
vivifying the source slot, a hash argument, a 100-element array, the callee
pushing to the array it was handed, mixed kinds, foreach-over-@_ aliasing, @_
passed on to a second sub).  Those rows pass on the BASE extraction too â they
are the net.  Fable's review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/
p1517-flatten.pl reads BYTE-IDENTICAL to main, and differs from perl only in
the three ways it already did (absent warnings, #155 tied arrays, A6's count).
Full sweep GATE clean, TOTAL 18686 (+0); companion op/ 10 files ROW DIFF
0/0/0/0; corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 (runtime-only, no generation bump).

THE PRE-SIZING ARM STAYS KILLED and its rejection comment is still above
p-flatten-args.  The per-array "every element is a box" FACT is NOT BUILT and
is no longer needed for this row: what it would buy on top of the bulk copy is
the patch pass, which is now one SVREF and one `p-box-p` per element over a
simple vector.  If a future measurement wants that last slice, the fact is
still the way â but it would have to beat a 2.7 ns per element baseline, not
the 9.0 ns one this task was filed against.
subject: PERF, BOTH HALVES DONE: `p-flatten-args` copies a whole-array argument in BULK (s473x: feargs 0.1854 -> 0.0551 s, +236.6 %, 9.0 ns -> 2.7 ns per element, 8.2x perl -> 2.5x) -- and the per-array "every element is a box" FACT turned out not to be needed: the cost was the hairy source read (33.6 %) and the one-at-a-time growth (~36 %), while the element promotion was 0.2 %
